title: Iowa National Guard MEDEVAC Rescue
description: A medevac aircrew from C Company, 2/211 General Aviation Support Battalion, Iowa National Guard, showcased their exceptional skills during a hoist rescue operation during flood search and rescue operations in Spencer, Iowa on June 22, 2024.  The team demonstrated seamless coordination and technical expertise, ensuring the swift and safe extraction of the individual in need. This mission highlights the dedication and readiness of our medevac teams to respond effectively in critical situations, underscoring their vital role in our community's safety and well-being. (U.S. Army National Guard video by Spc. Armani Wilson)
unit_name: Joint Force Headquarters - Iowa National Guard

transcript.text: So we were flying around , we see this
truck in the middle of the road and
we're like , there's no way somebody
can be in that truck right now . The
individual , we've seen him waving out
the , waving his arms . You know , we
swung around a little wind out of the
west . And with those power lines there ,
we came in to make sure we had a stable
hover and that led to our first rescue
hoist . He kind of gets like this .
Like I , I know how to do this . I do
this all the time . We practice this
over and over again . My job is I'm a
flight medic . So I got on to the hoist
and got hoisted down and landed on top
of the truck bed or the roof of the
truck . We put the rescue strap around
him and then we lifted him up into the
air and into the helicopter while he
was still on the hook , we got him into
the seat , make sure he was secure .
You know , he gave a thumbs up that he
was good to go . This is why I joined
and to be able to actually do what we
train for so often , especially with a
ho mission , you know , on planning on
top of a roof of a vehicle . It's not
just a one week in a month , two weeks
during the summer sort of situation .
There , there is a very heavy
commitment to this job , but we all
take a lot of pride in it and we like
being good at what we do .
